newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Charts signal more gains in Russian telecoms - MC.
newsitem.headline: Charts signal more gains in Russian telecoms - MC.

text.p: Russian telecom shares have performed well recently and look set to move higher according to a technical analysis, London investment bank MC Securities said.
Rostelekom, St Petersburg Telephone (PTS) and MGTS show most technical strength, it said in a report by analysts Natalia Ivanova and Stephen O'Sullivan, dated February 6.
"It would not be a surprise if East European and Russian telecom shares were one of the best performing sectors in the first half of 1997, due to their strong technical formations," it said.
Rostelekom is expected to make further gains and could hit $4.50 per share in the next few months, the report said.
PTS has steadily increased and could make further advances before reaching resistance of $1.80, it said.
MGTS shares continue to break new ground and are a "must have," it said. Resistance for MGTS was $1,000.

Regional telecom operators such as Samara Svyazinform and Kubanelektrosvyaz are moving higher, towards resistance at $70 and $24 respectively, but consolidation is needed to sustain the advance, it said.
But Nizhny Novgorod Svyazinform was facing resistance at $3, and could be confined to a sideways trading range, it said.
At 1130 GMT on Monday Rostelekom was $4.08 on the Russian Trading System (RTS), PTS was $1.46 and MGTS was already $1,400.
On Friday February 10 Samara Svyazinform traded at $61.50 on the RTS second tier, Kubanelektrosvyaz at $22.25 and Nizhny Novgorod Svyazinform at $2.82.
